limitations_and_boundaries: The study uses an LPS-induced systemic inflammation mouse model, which may not fully recapitulate all aspects of human PD.
The temporal analysis is limited to 1 day and 14 days post-LPS; intermediate time points are not examined for all parameters.
The in vitro coculture system uses a fixed 3:1 neuron-to-microglia ratio, which may not reflect in vivo cellular proportions.
The study does not explore the role of other complement components or phagocytic receptors beyond CR3.
The potential off-target effects of AAV-mediated CR3 knockdown in microglia are not fully addressed.
The study does not investigate the long-term functional consequences of CR3 inhibition on motor or cognitive behavior.
The findings are based on a single LPS regimen; different doses or durations of systemic inflammation may yield different outcomes.
The role of peripheral immune cells infiltrating the CNS is not examined.
The study does not assess the impact of CR3 knockdown on other glial cells such as astrocytes.
The molecular mechanisms downstream of CR3 activation in microglia are not elucidated.
